findings.title: Configuration provides no visible route to the second-screen destination
findings.evidence: src/pages.js:880-928 renders the configuration surface with Save, Install, account connection and a manifest endpoint footer, but no watch URL or action. The saved notice at lines 890-892 directs only installation. The route can instead be found in native tray actions at src-tauri/src/lib.rs:327-340 or after activation at src/pages.js:1180-1193. The factual packet independently records no visible route to the waiting player on /configure.
findings.necessary_complexity: partly-avoidable: installation in Stremio and source selection remain necessary; searching another surface for the stable viewer destination is avoidable
findings.user_effect: A new host preparing another device must find the tray or first select content to locate the viewer URL, despite already being on the setup surface. This predicts extra navigation, not measured task failure.
findings.correction: Add a compact next-steps area after source setup that exposes the stable second-screen URL with copy/open actions and identifies selecting a Unilink result in Stremio as the source-selection step.
findings.verify: On a clean profile, save a valid source configuration and locate the second-screen URL directly on the resulting page without returning to the tray or selecting content; copying and opening it should reach the waiting player. Preserve the existing source input and installation action.

keep: Activation places the selected title, destination URL, copy and open actions together before subtitle settings (src/pages.js:1170-1200).

findings.title: Setup instructions and the source to select use different names
findings.evidence: src/pages.js:899 describes the installed action as Servir en red, and src/pages.js:1321 asks the waiting viewer to choose that label. src/streams.js:361 generates the source name as Unilink followed by its quality label. The supplied polish-evidence.md also records the waiting instruction at runtime. Thus the novice must infer that a differently named Stremio result is the instructed action; actual user confusion was not measured.
findings.necessary_complexity: Partly avoidable: selecting a quality/source in a separate Stremio application is required by the product, but translating two names for the same source is unnecessary.
findings.user_effect: Predicted extra cross-referencing between setup or waiting instructions and Stremio results, with possible hesitation about whether installation produced the right add-on.
findings.correction: Use the emitted name Unilink in configuration and waiting instructions, with a short qualifier that the source may also show its quality. Keep the same terminology in the install-to-selection handoff.
findings.verify: Render configuration and empty watch pages and a decorated stream fixture; verify that both instructions name the actual Unilink prefix. In a safe Stremio walkthrough, confirm the named result can be identified without translating a second action label. This verifies consistency, not measured workload reduction.

findings.title: Tray conflates intentional stop, startup, and failed startup
findings.evidence: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:184-220 derives menu text solely from whether the HTTP health probe succeeds: Servidor activo or Servidor detenido. Start/restart errors at lines 283-300 are only printed to stderr; child termination at lines 153-165 drops the process without retaining a failure cause. open_onboarding_when_ready at lines 247-268 silently stops trying after twenty readiness polls. A host sees the same stopped state after a deliberate stop and a failed attempted start.
findings.necessary_complexity: partly-avoidable: users need to distinguish an externally owned server and deliberate interruption; inferring whether their start request is still progressing or has failed is avoidable.
findings.user_effect: Predicted uncertainty about whether the command was received or another start attempt is appropriate, with possible repeated clicks and no confidence that onboarding will appear. No such human behavior was measured.
findings.correction: Retain explicit starting and failed states for owned lifecycle operations, show a short safe failure explanation in the tray or a reachable local status surface, and clear failure only after a new operation or verified readiness. Preserve external-server ownership gating.
findings.verify: With isolated native fixtures, invoke a delayed start and a forced spawn/bind failure. Observe starting immediately, then active only after health succeeds or a distinguishable failure outcome. Deliberate stop must continue to say stopped. Verify a later successful retry clears the prior failure.

findings.title: Source selection has no app acknowledgment until optional preparation completes
findings.evidence: src/server.js:781-819 changes the active registry source, then awaits Promise.all(loadActiveSubtitles, prepareSeriesMarathon) before sending activationPage. The selected source is already active, but the app provides no handoff page or preparation state while these external requests complete. The browser may show its generic loading indication; that does not explain that selection succeeded and optional preparation is pending.
findings.necessary_complexity: partly-avoidable: fetching subtitle and episode metadata takes legitimate asynchronous work; withholding confirmation of the already-selected source is avoidable.
findings.user_effect: Predicted uncertainty over whether Stremio handed off the source successfully and whether the user should wait or select again. This is a latency-sensitive risk, not evidence of observed duplicate selection or task failure.
findings.correction: Acknowledge selection promptly with the source and stable watch address, and report optional preparation as pending and subsequently complete or partially unavailable. Keep later updates bound to the selected source instance so old preparation cannot misreport a newer selection.
findings.verify: Delay subtitle/metadata fixture responses. Confirm that the handoff immediately identifies the accepted source and offers the watch address, then updates preparation status without reactivating the source. Fail optional preparation and confirm a useful partial-success message while current playback remains available.

Native controls distinguish owned and externally running servers for stop/restart availability; preserve that meaningful constraint.

Exercise startup failure and delayed readiness in the native installed application; code establishes state collapse but not the OS presentation of all launch failures.

findings.title: Failed server start leaves no actionable diagnosis in the recovery surface
findings.evidence: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:115-166 propagates filesystem/sidecar spawn errors, and handles child termination without retaining a reason. Start/restart handlers at lines 283-300 print errors only to stderr. apply_menu_state at lines 198-221 exposes only active/stopped and enables another start. open_onboarding_when_ready at lines 247-265 silently ends after readiness retries. Thus an operator with a failed start can retry but cannot obtain the failure cause or a targeted recovery step from the tray.
findings.necessary_complexity: partly-avoidable: resolving a missing sidecar, inaccessible data directory, or unavailable port inherently needs different action; making the operator diagnose these without a visible bounded cause is avoidable.
findings.user_effect: Predicted repeated start attempts or outside support/log investigation before the host can restore service; no measured delay or inability to complete is claimed.
findings.correction: Retain a bounded sanitized startup/termination failure state and expose it with a concrete next step beside the tray retry action. Preserve the tray after initial failure, distinguish intentional stop, and clear the failure after a verified successful start.
findings.verify: With disposable native fixtures, cause missing-sidecar and occupied-port startup failures. Verify that the tray remains available, identifies an actionable reason, offers retry, preserves configuration, and returns to running after correcting the fixture and retrying. Also verify intentional stop is not labeled a failure.

keep: Configuration validation/save failure preserves the submitted manifest URL and provides an inline alert; src/server.js:710-724 and src/pages.js:888-912.
Expired activation explains returning to Stremio to reopen the movie; src/streams.js:192-195. Preserve that specific recovery instruction.
Tray stop/restart controls are gated by owned process state, and persistent host configuration survives normal server restart.
unknowns: Native error discoverability and actual recovery effectiveness require a safe runtime failure probe; code evidence alone does not establish user comprehension.
Browser form submission was a documented verification gap, so no form-recovery defect is attributed to that observation.
cross_refs: Uncertainty: the same native stopped label does not explain whether a start failed; the Recovery finding concerns restoring progress through a targeted corrective action.
Search/Integration: onboarding terminology and next-step visibility belong to those assessors unless a distinct failed-state reconstruction cost is established.
